history.content: The temple was demolished by Muslim rulers during 1422–1436 AD (Rustumdil Khan, the Subedar of Hyderabad, with the support of Aurangzeb, is said to have converted it to a mosque), and was rebuilt in the 17th century, regaining its status as a major Vaishnava shrine. The Kottha (New) Narasimha Swamy Temple, also known as Sri Ugra Narasimha Swamy Temple, was built in 1803 AD by Panatula Narayana Deekshitulu and stands to the right of the Pata Narasimha temple. The temple is administered by the Telangana Endowments Department (one of 19 major temples with annual income above ₹1 crore, per the 2015 Trust Board notification). For the 2027 Godavari Pushkaralu, the Telangana government has allocated ₹50 crore for renovation, including ₹80 lakh for a new toilet complex and ₹3.1 crore for four VIP suites. The temple is a major centre for Vedic Brahmin scholars in Telangana and one of the nine Nava Narasimha Kshetrams.

summary: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple (Dharmapuri Kshetram) in Dharmapuri, Jagtial District, Telangana, is an ancient Narasimha shrine (built c. 850–928 AD / 1018 AD per inscriptions; rebuilt multiple times) on the southern bank of the Dakshina Vahini Godavari River, where the Godavari uniquely flows southward. One of the nine Nava Narasimha Kshetrams and a 'Hari-Hara Kshetra', it houses the rare Padmasana-form of Lakshmi Narasimha with Goddess Lakshmi, plus shrines to Ugra/Yoga/Saumya Narasimha forms, Lord Venkateswara, Lord Brahma (rare 6-ft, four-faced murti), eight Hanumans, and Lord Yama. The town has both a Pata (Old) and a Kottha (New) Narasimha temple from cycles of destruction and reconstruction (the Kottha built in 1803 AD by Panatula Narayana Deekshitulu). It is busiest during the 13-day Brahmotsavam (Phalguna Shuddha Ekadashi to Ashtami, Feb/Mar), Narasimha Jayanthi, Vaikuntha Ekadashi and the Godavari Pushkaralu (next: 2027).

answer.answer: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple in Dharmapuri has ancient roots dating back to the 11th‑century Chalukyas. It was destroyed in the early 15th century by Muslim rulers, rebuilt in the 17th century, and the New Narasimha shrine was added in 1803 by Panatula Narayana Deekshitulu. Recent reconstruction by the Telangana government preserved the original cave shrine and elevated the site to a major spiritual landmark. Legends credit King Dharma Varma, Lord Rama, and references in the Skanda and Brahmanda Puranas, linking the shrine to Narasimha’s post‑Hiranyakashipu meditation. The temple is one of the nine Nava Narasimha Kshetrams and is administered by the Telangana Endowments Department.

claims.claim: The original Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple dates back to the 11th century CE under the Chalukya dynasty.
The temple was demolished by Muslim rulers between 1422–1436 AD, with Rustumdil Khan and Aurangzeb, and was converted into a mosque.
The temple was rebuilt in the 17th century, restoring its status as a major Vaishnava shrine.
The Kottha (New Narasimha) temple was built in 1803 AD by Panatula Narayana Deekshitulu.
The Government of Telangana undertook a reconstruction project preserving the original cave shrine and making the temple one of India's grandest spiritual landmarks.

Legends attribute the foundation to King Dharma Varma, recount that Lord Rama visited the site, mention the temple in Skanda and Brahmanda Puranas, and link the shrine to Narasimha’s meditation after slaying Hiranyakashipu.
The temple is one of the nine Nava Narasimha Kshetrams and is administered by the Telangana Endowments Department.

faq.answer: It is famous for being one of the nine Nava Narasimha Kshetrams, for its location on the sacred Dakshina Vahini (southward-flowing) Godavari River, for being called 'Dakshina Kashi' (Southern Varanasi) and 'Teertharajamu' (king of pilgrimages), for the rare Padmasana-form of Lord Lakshmi Narasimha, and for its status as a Hari-Hara Kshetra (Vaishnava-Shaiva harmony). The town has one of the largest settlements of Vedic Brahmins in Telangana. The next Godavari Pushkaralu is 26 June – 7 July 2027.
faq.id: FAQ004
faq.question: What are the temple timings?
faq.answer: Per the JustDial official listing and dharmapurikshetram.in: 5:30 AM–2:30 PM and 4:00 PM–8:00 PM daily. The temple opens with Suprabhata Seva at 5:00 AM. Some other sources (Tripadvisor, Trawell, Grokipedia) give 5:00 AM–2:00 PM and 4:00 PM–8:00 PM. The 2:30 PM–4:00 PM break for darshanam is confirmed. Hours are extended during the 13-day Brahmotsavam, Narasimha Jayanthi, Vaikuntha Ekadashi and Godavari Pushkaralu.

answer.answer: At the Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple in Dharmapuri, daily darshan begins at 5:30 AM, continues until 2:30 PM, takes a 2:30–4:00 PM break, then resumes from 4:00–8:00 PM; the Suprabhata Seva starts at 5:00 AM, and during festivals (Brahmotsavam, Narasimha Jayanthi, Vaikuntha Ekadashi, Godavari Pushkaralu) the hours are extended. At the Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple in Yadagirigutta, the temple opens at 3:30 AM and offers a sequence of early‑morning sevas (Suprabhatam 3:30–4:00 AM, Thiruvaradhana 4:00–4:30 AM, Bala Bogam 4:30–5:15 AM, Nijabhishekam 5:15–6:15 AM, Archana 6:15–7:00 AM), followed by Sarva Darshan windows (7:00–9:00 AM, 10:00–11:45 AM, 12:30–3:00 PM, 5:00–7:00 PM, 8:15–9:00 PM) and VIP Break Darshan slots (9:00–10:00 AM and 4:00–5:00 PM); Sarva Darshan is free while VIP Break Darshan is paid.

Following its grand reconstruction, Yadadri has emerged as one of India's finest pilgrimage destinations, attracting millions of devotees each year with its spiritual significance, magnificent architecture, and world-class facilities.

answer.answer: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple, also known as Yadadri Temple, is a revered Vaishnavite shrine in Telangana. It is considered one of the most sacred Narasimha Kshetrams and one of the holiest Pancha Narasimha Kshetrams. The temple houses five divine manifestations of Lord Narasimha—Jwala, Gandabherunda, Yogananda, Ugra, and Lakshmi—each believed to offer protection, compassion, and spiritual power. The original cave shrine, where Lord Narasimha appeared to Sage Yadarishi, is particularly sacred. Devotees visit to seek blessings for health, marriage, education, and prosperity, and many report miracles such as relief from fear, health issues, financial hardships, and family disputes. The temple attracts millions of pilgrims annually and has recently undergone a grand reconstruction that preserved its historic cave shrine.

overview: Sri Sita Ramachandra Swamy Temple, popularly known as Bhadrachalam Temple, is one of the most revered pilgrimage destinations dedicated to Lord Sri Rama in India. Located on the serene banks of the sacred Godavari River in Bhadradri Kothagudem district of Telangana, it is regarded as the spiritual heart of Rama devotion in South India and is affectionately called Dakshina Ayodhya ('Ayodhya of the South'). The deity appears in the rare Vaikuntha Rama form with four divine arms. The temple is deeply connected with the legendary devotee Bhakta Ramadasu (Kancharla Gopanna) and attracts millions of devotees every year.
summary: Sri Sita Ramachandra Swamy Temple, popularly known as Bhadrachalam Temple, is one of India's most revered temples dedicated to Lord Sri Rama. Located on the banks of the Godavari River in Bhadradri Kothagudem district of Telangana, the temple is celebrated for its association with the Ramayana, Bhakta Bhadra, and Bhakta Ramadasu. It attracts millions of devotees every year, particularly during Sri Rama Navami, when the celestial wedding of Lord Rama and Sita (Sri Sita Rama Kalyanam) is performed. Known for its unique Vaikuntha Rama idol, rich historical significance, grand festivals, sacred rituals, and well-organized pilgrim facilities, it is one of the most visited pilgrimage destinations in South India.

overview: Sri Sita Ramachandra Swamy Temple, popularly known as Bhadrachalam Temple, is one of the most revered pilgrimage destinations dedicated to Lord Sri Rama in India. Located on the serene banks of the sacred Godavari River in Bhadradri Kothagudem district of Telangana, it is regarded as the spiritual heart of Rama devotion in South India and is affectionately called Dakshina Ayodhya ('Ayodhya of the South'). The deity appears in the rare Vaikuntha Rama form with four divine arms. The temple is deeply connected with the legendary devotee Bhakta Ramadasu (Kancharla Gopanna) and attracts millions of devotees every year.
summary: Sri Sita Ramachandra Swamy Temple, popularly known as Bhadrachalam Temple, is one of India's most revered temples dedicated to Lord Sri Rama. Located on the banks of the Godavari River in Bhadradri Kothagudem district of Telangana, the temple is celebrated for its association with the Ramayana, Bhakta Bhadra, and Bhakta Ramadasu. It attracts millions of devotees every year, particularly during Sri Rama Navami, when the celestial wedding of Lord Rama and Sita (Sri Sita Rama Kalyanam) is performed. Known for its unique Vaikuntha Rama idol, rich historical significance, grand festivals, sacred rituals, and well-organized pilgrim facilities, it is one of the most visited pilgrimage destinations in South India.

travel_tips: Vehicles can be driven up to the temple entrance, saving the climb for those who wish.

overview: Sri Raja Rajeshwara Swamy Devasthanam at Vemulawada, Rajanna Sircilla District, Telangana, is an ancient Shaivite shrine dedicated to Lord Raja Rajeshwara (a form of Lord Shiva), worshipped as the Neela Lohitha Siva Lingam. Revered as 'Dakshina Kasi' (the Kashi of the South), 'Harihara Kshetram' (both Shiva and Vishnu worshipped in one complex), and 'Bhaskara Kshetram', the temple's origins are lost in antiquity and it was historically the capital of the Vemulawada Chalukyas (c. 750–973 CE). It is famed for its signature Kode Mrokkubadi ritual and the curative Dharmagundam tank.
summary: Sri Raja Rajeshwara Swamy Devasthanam (Vemulawada Temple) is an ancient Shiva temple in Rajanna Sircilla District, Telangana, where the presiding deity is locally called 'Rajanna'. Venerated as Dakshina Kasi, Harihara Kshetram and Bhaskara Kshetram, it blends Shaivite and Vaishnavite worship within one complex. Historically the capital of the Vemulawada Chalukyas (c. 750–973 CE), the temple is renowned for the Kode Mrokkubadi ritual, the Dharmagundam holy tank, Maha Shivaratri (its principal festival), and Maha Lingarchana. It draws large pilgrim crowds year-round.

It draws large pilgrim crowds year-round.

overview: Sri Raja Rajeshwara Swamy Devasthanam at Vemulawada, Rajanna Sircilla District, Telangana, is an ancient Shaivite shrine dedicated to Lord Raja Rajeshwara (a form of Lord Shiva), worshipped as the Neela Lohitha Siva Lingam. Revered as 'Dakshina Kasi' (the Kashi of the South), 'Harihara Kshetram' (both Shiva and Vishnu worshipped in one complex), and 'Bhaskara Kshetram', the temple's origins are lost in antiquity and it was historically the capital of the Vemulawada Chalukyas (c. 750–973 CE). It is famed for its signature Kode Mrokkubadi ritual and the curative Dharmagundam tank.
summary: Sri Raja Rajeshwara Swamy Devasthanam (Vemulawada Temple) is an ancient Shiva temple in Rajanna Sircilla District, Telangana, where the presiding deity is locally called 'Rajanna'. Venerated as Dakshina Kasi, Harihara Kshetram and Bhaskara Kshetram, it blends Shaivite and Vaishnavite worship within one complex. Historically the capital of the Vemulawada Chalukyas (c. 750–973 CE), the temple is renowned for the Kode Mrokkubadi ritual, the Dharmagundam holy tank, Maha Shivaratri (its principal festival), and Maha Lingarchana. It draws large pilgrim crowds year-round.

faq.answer: Because of its antiquity, Puranic references and status as a major Shaivite pilgrimage centre in South India, devotees consider a visit here to carry spiritual merit comparable to a pilgrimage to Kashi (Varanasi).
faq.id: FAQ006
faq.question: How far is the temple from Hyderabad, and how do I get there?
faq.answer: Approximately 150 km by road via Siddipet and Sircilla (NH563), roughly 3.5–4 hours by car or TSRTC bus.
faq.id: FAQ007
faq.question: Is accommodation available at the temple?
faq.answer: Yes. The Devasthanam operates several guest-house cottages and satrams with AC and non-AC rooms at reported tariffs ranging from about ₹50 (dormitory/satram) to ₹2,000 (AC suite) per day.
faq.id: FAQ008
faq.question: What is the dress code for pujas like Abhishekam?
faq.answer: For pujas such as Abhishekam, men are typically required to remove shirt/vest during the ritual; a traditional dhoti/pancha is recommended. General darshan allows any decent traditional or modern attire.
faq.id: FAQ009
faq.question: What is the best time of year to visit?
faq.answer: October to March (and often extended to early June) is generally recommended for pleasant weather; Mondays and the Maha Shivaratri period are the most spiritually significant but also the most crowded.

It stands as one of only two major Saraswati temples in the Indian subcontinent and the sole temple in South India devoted to this deity. The temple is renowned for its Aksharabhyasam ceremony, initiating children into learning, and devotees believe that worship here brings success in education and intellectual pursuits. The site features a miraculous Vedavathi monolith, associated with legends of Sage Vedavyasa consecrating the sand idols of Saraswati, Lakshmi, and Kali/Gowri after the Kurukshetra War. Major festivals such as Vasantha Panchami, Maha Shivaratri, and Devi Navaratrulu draw thousands of pilgrims.

overview: Sri Kondagattu Anjaneya Swamy Temple is one of the most cherished and spiritually potent Hanuman temples in Telangana. Nestled on a picturesque hillock enveloped by lush forests and flowing streams, close to Kondagattu village in Mallial Mandal, Jagtial district, it is dedicated to Lord Anjaneya (Hanuman). The temple is renowned as a divine-healing shrine providing relief from Shani Dosha, fear, mental stress, legal issues, and negative planetary influences. For generations, devotees from Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Karnataka have flocked here in search of strength, courage, and divine protection.
summary: Sri Kondagattu Anjaneya Swamy Temple is a historic Hanuman temple in Muthyampet village, Mallial Mandal, Jagtial District, Telangana. Per local tradition it is associated with the Treta Yuga (Lord Hanuman pausing here while carrying the Sanjeevani mountain), while the present shrine is said to have been founded ~300 years ago by a cowherd guided by a vision of Hanuman and later renovated ~160 years ago by Krishna Rao Deshmukh. The complex features two large Anjaneya idols and shrines to Venkateswara, Lakshmi, Rama, Sita, Lakshmana and Shiva. It is famed for Shani Dosha relief, a believed 40-day puja for childless couples, and Hanuman Jayanti, which draws an estimated 4 lakh devotees annually.

sthala_puranam: The name 'Kondagattu' is derived from the Telugu words 'Konda' (hill) and 'Gattu' (embankment or edge), capturing the temple's hilltop location. Per local tradition, while carrying the Sanjeevani mountain to revive Lakshmana, Lord Hanuman passed over the Mutyampeta region and a fragment of the mountain became the present-day Kondagattu hill, where he paused to rest. The lush forest around offered medicinal herbs, and sages later installed the idol here. Per Telangana360, about 300 years ago a cowherd named Singam Sanjeevudu, after losing one of his buffalos, came to this hillock searching for it and slept here. Lord Anjaneya came into his dream and told him the whereabouts of his buffalo. As he woke up and looked around the hillock, he found an illuminating idol of Anjaneya, and he then built a small temple for the lord at the current location.

Section: overview

overview: Sri Jogulamba Devi Temple, popularly known as Jogulamba Temple, is one of the most sacred Shakti temples in India. Located at Alampur in Jogulamba Gadwal district of Telangana, near the confluence of the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers, it is revered as one of the 18 Maha Shakti Peethas and the Western Gateway (Paschima Dwaram) of the Srisailam Temple. The name 'Jogulamba' comes from the Telugu 'Yogula Amma' meaning 'Mother of Yogis'. The Goddess is worshipped in her fierce Ugra form for protection, courage, prosperity, and spiritual enlightenment. The temple stands adjacent to the 7th-century Bala Brahmeswara Swamy Temple and the Navabrahma Temples of the Badami Chalukya dynasty.
summary: Sri Jogulamba Devi Temple at Alampur, Telangana, is one of the 18 Maha Shakti Peethas — where, per tradition, the upper teeth of Goddess Sati fell. Dedicated to Goddess Jogulamba (a fierce form of Parvati), it lies near the confluence of the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers and serves as the Western Gateway (Paschima Dwaram) of Srisailam Temple. The original 7th-century Badami Chalukya temple was destroyed in the 14th century by Bahmani invaders; the idol was safeguarded in the Bala Brahmeswara Temple for centuries and was ceremoniously reinstalled at the reconstructed temple in 2005. Today it is one of the most visited Shakti Peethas in South India, especially during Sharannavaratri.

overview: Sri Jogulamba Devi Temple, popularly known as Jogulamba Temple, is one of the most sacred Shakti temples in India. Located at Alampur in Jogulamba Gadwal district of Telangana, near the confluence of the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers, it is revered as one of the 18 Maha Shakti Peethas and the Western Gateway (Paschima Dwaram) of the Srisailam Temple. The name 'Jogulamba' comes from the Telugu 'Yogula Amma' meaning 'Mother of Yogis'. The Goddess is worshipped in her fierce Ugra form for protection, courage, prosperity, and spiritual enlightenment. The temple stands adjacent to the 7th-century Bala Brahmeswara Swamy Temple and the Navabrahma Temples of the Badami Chalukya dynasty.
summary: Sri Jogulamba Devi Temple at Alampur, Telangana, is one of the 18 Maha Shakti Peethas — where, per tradition, the upper teeth of Goddess Sati fell. Dedicated to Goddess Jogulamba (a fierce form of Parvati), it lies near the confluence of the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers and serves as the Western Gateway (Paschima Dwaram) of Srisailam Temple. The original 7th-century Badami Chalukya temple was destroyed in the 14th century by Bahmani invaders; the idol was safeguarded in the Bala Brahmeswara Temple for centuries and was ceremoniously reinstalled at the reconstructed temple in 2005. Today it is one of the most visited Shakti Peethas in South India, especially during Sharannavaratri.

architecture: The temple is a beautiful blend of traditional South Indian temple architecture and modern design. Reconstructed in 2005 at its original location in the Chalukyan style to complement the nearby ancient Navabrahma Temples, the complex features a magnificent entrance, spacious mandapams, and beautifully carved pillars. The sanctum houses the fierce idol of Goddess Jogulamba in her Ugra Roopa — seated on a corpse with disheveled hair, a protruding tongue, and a scorpion, frog and lizard adorning her hair. A water pool surrounds the temple, creating a cool atmosphere. Adjacent are the ancient Bala Brahmeswara Swamy Temple and the Navabrahma Temples. The premises are clean, well-maintained and surrounded by gardens. Ashta Dasha Shakti Peeta's display is on Temple Pillars, and a Yagna Shala is also part of the complex.

history.content: The temple's history dates back more than a thousand years and is closely associated with ancient Shaivite traditions. history.founders: Kakatiya dynasty (flourished/renovated)

history.section: Yama Legend
history.content: According to temple legends, Lord Yama, the God of Death, installed the Shiva Linga of Lord Kaleshwara at this sacred site after worshipping Lord Mukteswara to seek liberation from the burden of taking away human lives. Because Lord Yama himself performed penance here, devotees believe worshipping at Kaleshwaram frees them from the fear of death and grants spiritual liberation.

answer.answer: Sri Kaleshwara Mukteswara Swamy Devasthanam is a Shaivite temple in Telangana that houses two Shiva lingas symbolizing liberation and protection from the cycle of birth and death. According to legend, Lord Yama installed the Kaleshwara linga. Worship here is believed to relieve Kaala Sarpa Dosha, bring healing, remove obstacles, improve health and prosperity, and provide spiritual peace. The Mukteswara linga has two nostril-like openings that allow abhishekam water to flow into the Triveni Sangamam, considered a divine blessing. Pitru Karmas performed at the Sangamam bring peace to departed souls. Maha Shivaratri, Karthika Masam and Shravana Masam are considered most auspicious times to visit.

claims.claim: The temple houses two Shiva lingas that symbolize liberation (moksha) and protection from the cycle of birth and death.
Lord Yama, the God of Death, is associated with the temple and is said to have installed the Kaleshwara Linga.

The Mukteswara Linga has two nostril-like openings that allow abhishekam water to flow into the Triveni Sangamam, considered a divine blessing.

history.section: Historical Background
history.content: Chilkur Balaji Temple is regarded as one of the oldest temples in the Hyderabad/Ranga Reddy region. Wikipedia's infobox records the structure as completed in the 14th century, while tourism sources (including the Ranga Reddy District government page) describe it as built 'half a millennium ago'. It is said to have been built during the era of Akkanna and Madanna, ministers under the Qutub Shahi (Golconda) administration and uncles of the Bhakti-poet Ramadas of Bhadrachalam. In 1963, the year following the Sino-Indian border conflict, the idol of the temple's goddess (Ammavaru) was installed and named 'Rajya Lakshmi' to mark the restoration of peace.

Lord Venkateswara appeared to him in a dream saying, 'I am right here in the jungle nearby; you do not have to worry.' The devotee went to the spot shown, found a mole-hill and dug into it; his axe accidentally struck a buried idol, causing it to 'bleed', after which a voice instructed him to bathe the mound in cow's milk. Doing so revealed a Swayambhu idol of Lord Balaji flanked by Sridevi and Bhoodevi, and a temple was built to house it.

Lord Venkateswara appeared to him in a dream saying, 'I am right here in the jungle nearby; you do not have to worry.' The devotee went to the spot shown, found a mole-hill and dug into it; his axe accidentally struck a buried idol, causing it to 'bleed', after which a voice instructed him to bathe the mound in cow's milk. Doing so revealed a Swayambhu idol of Lord Balaji flanked by Sridevi and Bhoodevi, and a temple was built to house it.

overview: Chilkur Balaji Temple (Sri Balaji Venkateswara Swamy Temple), popularly known as the 'Visa Balaji Temple', is one of the oldest temples in the Hyderabad/Ranga Reddy region, located at Chilkur Village on the banks of Osman Sagar, off Vikarabad Road. The presiding deity is a Swayambhu (self-manifested) idol of Lord Balaji Venkateswara flanked by Sridevi and Bhoodevi. The temple is uniquely run by hereditary trustees/archakas (Dr. M.V. Soundara Rajan, C.S. Gopala Krishna, and current head priest C.S. Rangarajan) and operates independently of the state Endowments Department. It is celebrated for having no hundi (donation box), accepting no monetary donations, and offering no VIP or paid special darshan — every devotee follows the same queue. Its defining practice is 11 pradakshinas while making a wish and 108 once the wish is fulfilled.

summary: Chilkur Balaji Temple in Ranga Reddy District, Telangana, is a 14th-century (per Wikipedia) Vaishnavite shrine to a Swayambhu idol of Lord Balaji Venkateswara with Sridevi and Bhoodevi. Popularly called 'Visa Balaji' because devotees flock here to pray for overseas visa success, it is one of India's very few trustee-managed temples that won legal autonomy from the state Endowments Department (2008). It charges no fees — no hundi, no donations, no VIP darshan — and its core ritual is the 11/108 pradakshina vow. Principal festival: the seven-day Brahmotsavam in Chaitra (March/April).

religious_significance: Chilkur Balaji is regarded as an accessible manifestation of Lord Venkateswara ('Pratyaksha Daiva' of the Kali Yuga) for those unable to travel to Tirumala Tirupati. Its defining devotional practice is 11 pradakshinas of the inner shrine while making a wish, followed by 108 pradakshinas once the wish is fulfilled. The temple is distinguished by two verified features: it has no hundi and accepts no monetary donations, and it provides no VIP or expedited darshan — all devotees follow the same queue.
spiritual_significance: The temple's best-known belief is its association with success in visa applications for overseas travel, study or work (hence 'Visa Balaji'). Devotees also seek blessings for employment, marriage and (via the Friday Garuda Prasadam) for children. These are devotional beliefs reported in tourism and news sources; they are not medical, legal, or immigration guarantees.

overview: Birla Mandir is one of the most prominent Hindu temples in Hyderabad, Telangana. Dedicated to Lord Sri Venkateswara (Balaji), the temple stands atop Naubat Pahad, overlooking the city and Hussain Sagar Lake. Constructed entirely of white Rajasthan marble (about 2,000 tons), it is renowned for its peaceful atmosphere, architectural beauty, and panoramic views of Hyderabad. Built by the Birla Foundation (1970–1976) under the guidance of Swami Ranganathananda of the Ramakrishna Mission, it blends Dravidian, Rajasthani, and Utkala architectural styles. Every year, thousands of devotees and tourists visit to seek blessings and admire its magnificent craftsmanship.
summary: Birla Mandir, atop Naubat Pahad in Khairatabad, Hyderabad, is a prominent Vaishnavite temple dedicated to Lord Sri Venkateswara (Balaji). Built entirely of pure white Rajasthan marble by the Birla Foundation between 1970 and 1976 under Swami Ranganathananda of the Ramakrishna Mission, it harmoniously blends Dravidian, Rajasthani and Utkala architecture, with intricate carvings from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Bhagavad Gita. The sanctum houses an ~11-foot granite idol of Lord Venkateswara, with additional shrines to Padmavati, Andal, Shiva, Lakshmi, Ganesha, Hanuman and Sai Baba. It is a major centre of Vaishnavite worship and a popular tourist landmark overlooking Hussain Sagar.

overview: Birla Mandir is one of the most prominent Hindu temples in Hyderabad, Telangana. Dedicated to Lord Sri Venkateswara (Balaji), the temple stands atop Naubat Pahad, overlooking the city and Hussain Sagar Lake. Constructed entirely of white Rajasthan marble (about 2,000 tons), it is renowned for its peaceful atmosphere, architectural beauty, and panoramic views of Hyderabad. Built by the Birla Foundation (1970–1976) under the guidance of Swami Ranganathananda of the Ramakrishna Mission, it blends Dravidian, Rajasthani, and Utkala architectural styles. Every year, thousands of devotees and tourists visit to seek blessings and admire its magnificent craftsmanship.
summary: Birla Mandir, atop Naubat Pahad in Khairatabad, Hyderabad, is a prominent Vaishnavite temple dedicated to Lord Sri Venkateswara (Balaji). Built entirely of pure white Rajasthan marble by the Birla Foundation between 1970 and 1976 under Swami Ranganathananda of the Ramakrishna Mission, it harmoniously blends Dravidian, Rajasthani and Utkala architecture, with intricate carvings from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Bhagavad Gita. The sanctum houses an ~11-foot granite idol of Lord Venkateswara, with additional shrines to Padmavati, Andal, Shiva, Lakshmi, Ganesha, Hanuman and Sai Baba. It is a major centre of Vaishnavite worship and a popular tourist landmark overlooking Hussain Sagar.

evidence.content:
Temple: Birla Mandir Hyderabad
Temple ID: T0009
Section: overview

overview: Birla Mandir is one of the most prominent Hindu temples in Hyderabad, Telangana. Dedicated to Lord Sri Venkateswara (Balaji), the temple stands atop Naubat Pahad, overlooking the city and Hussain Sagar Lake. Constructed entirely of white Rajasthan marble (about 2,000 tons), it is renowned for its peaceful atmosphere, architectural beauty, and panoramic views of Hyderabad. Built by the Birla Foundation (1970–1976) under the guidance of Swami Ranganathananda of the Ramakrishna Mission, it blends Dravidian, Rajasthani, and Utkala architectural styles. Every year, thousands of devotees and tourists visit to seek blessings and admire its magnificent craftsmanship.
summary: Birla Mandir, atop Naubat Pahad in Khairatabad, Hyderabad, is a prominent Vaishnavite temple dedicated to Lord Sri Venkateswara (Balaji). Built entirely of pure white Rajasthan marble by the Birla Foundation between 1970 and 1976 under Swami Ranganathananda of the Ramakrishna Mission, it harmoniously blends Dravidian, Rajasthani and Utkala architecture, with intricate carvings from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Bhagavad Gita. The sanctum houses an ~11-foot granite idol of Lord Venkateswara, with additional shrines to Padmavati, Andal, Shiva, Lakshmi, Ganesha, Hanuman and Sai Baba. It is a major centre of Vaishnavite worship and a popular tourist landmark overlooking Hussain Sagar.
